subQuestions.questionText:
The shareholders of … preference shares are compensated for past unpaid dividends due to low profits.
A. participating
B. redeemable
C. convertible
D. cumulative
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Cumulative preference shareholders are entitled to receive any unpaid dividends from previous years (when profits were too low) before any dividends are paid to ordinary shareholders.

subQuestions.questionText:
Employers and employees each contribute 1% of their basic wages to the …
A. Unemployment Insurance Fund.
B. Compensation Fund.
C. Road Accident Fund.
D. Fidelity Insurance Fund.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
The Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) is funded by 1% contributions from both employers and employees on basic wages.

subQuestions.questionText:
Mbali, a sales consultant, should … in order to improve her next presentation.
A. maintain good relationships with the audience
B. revise the objectives that were not achieved
C. present together with her colleagues
D. ignore criticism from the audience
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Reviewing/revising objectives that were not achieved during a presentation is the standard improvement step for the next presentation. The other options do not directly address improving future performance.

options.A: maintain good relationships with the audience
options.B: revise the objectives that were not achieved

subQuestions.questionText:
Team dynamic theories enable businesses to …
A. allocate tasks according to the roles of team members.
B. specialise in the production of quality products.
C. improve their public relations with communities.
D. provide training programmes to employees.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
Team dynamic theories help businesses to allocate tasks according to the roles, strengths and behaviours of team members.

options.A: allocate tasks according to the roles of team members.
options.B: specialise in the production of quality products.
options.C: improve their public relations with communities.

subQuestions.questionText:
Grey Manufacturing encourages employees to recycle waste material. This refers to … as an element of triple bottom line.
A. people
B. profit
C. planet
D. productivity
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Recycling of waste material relates to the Planet element of the Triple Bottom Line (environmental sustainability).

subQuestions.questionText: Complete the statement using the word(s) provided in the list (manager; communication; decision-making; compound; complainer; problem-solving; simple; leader; collaboration; expert): The … is responsible for the administration of tasks and programmes to reach set targets.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: manager (2 marks)
The manager (not the leader) administers tasks and programmes to reach set targets. Leaders inspire/influence; managers administer.

subQuestions.questionText: Complete the statement using the word(s) provided in the list: Calculation of … interest is based only on the original amount invested.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: simple (2 marks)
Simple interest is calculated only on the original (principal) amount invested, unlike compound interest which is calculated on principal plus accumulated interest.

subQuestions.questionText: Complete the statement using the word(s) provided in the list: Team members take part in decision-making to achieve their goals. This refers to … as a criterion for successful team performance.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: collaboration (2 marks)
Collaboration as a criterion for successful team performance refers to team members working together and participating in decision-making to achieve common goals.

subQuestions.questionText: Complete the statement using the word(s) provided in the list: Jacob deals with a/an … as a difficult personality by interrupting the situation and moving to the problem-solving process.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: complainer (2 marks)
A complainer as a difficult personality is dealt with by interrupting the complaining cycle and shifting the discussion to the problem-solving process.

subQuestions.questionText: Complete the statement using the word(s) provided in the list: The CEO of Moodley Accountants considered various alternatives before choosing the best one. This is known as …
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: decision-making (2 marks)
Decision-making is the process of considering various alternatives and selecting the best one.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a description from COLUMN B that matches 'Partnership' in COLUMN A. Options: A. obligation of businesses to declare all income received; B. enables businesses to have a competitive advantage as they render better services; C. shareholders receive dividends only if a profit is made; D. continuity of the business depends on the number of shareholders; E. employees make personal calls during working hours; F. enables businesses to recognise the needs of only one particular group of customers; G. incorporators receive dividends only after all shareholders have been paid; H. continuity of the business depends on the lifespan of the owners; I. employees use business resources for personal gain; J. obligation of every citizen to contribute towards the well-being of communities.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: H (2 marks)
A partnership has no separate legal personality, so the continuity of the business depends on the lifespan of the owners (partners).

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a description from COLUMN B that matches 'Founders' shares' in COLUMN A. (Same options A–J as above.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: G (2 marks)
Founders' shares are issued to the incorporators/promoters of a company; they receive dividends only after all other shareholders have been paid.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a description from COLUMN B that matches 'Social responsibility' in COLUMN A. (Same options A–J as above.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: J (2 marks)
Social responsibility refers to the obligation of every citizen (including businesses) to contribute towards the well-being of communities.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a description from COLUMN B that matches 'Abuse of work time' in COLUMN A. (Same options A–J as above.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: E (2 marks)
Abuse of work time refers to employees making personal calls (or other personal activities) during working hours.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose a description from COLUMN B that matches 'Diversity' in COLUMN A. (Same options A–J as above.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Diversity in the workplace enables businesses to have a competitive advantage as they can render better services to a wider range of customers.

subQuestions.questionText: Give any FOUR examples of long-term insurance.
subQuestions.memoText:
Examples of long-term insurance (mark first FOUR only, 1 mark each):
- Endowment policy
- Life cover policy/Life insurance
- Retirement annuity/Pension fund/Provident fund
- Disability policy
- Trauma insurance
- Funeral insurance
- Health insurance/Medical aid
- Any other relevant example related to long-term insurance.

subQuestions.questionText: Outline the rights of ordinary shareholders.
subQuestions.memoText:
Rights of ordinary shareholders (2 marks each, max 4):
Shareholders have a right to:
- Vote at the Annual General Meeting (AGM).
- Attend the AGM to learn about the company's performance.
- Receive interim and annual reports.
- Claim on company assets in the event of bankruptcy after all other creditors and preferential shareholders have been paid.
- Any other relevant answer related to the rights of ordinary shareholders.
[Max 4 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Read the scenario: 'Parker Dentistry (PD) has surplus funds and decided to invest a minimum amount of R1 000 as initial investment. They will be penalised if withdrawals are made within the first twelve months.' Identify the form of investment applicable in the scenario above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Government/RSA Retail Savings Bonds (2 marks)
The minimum initial investment of R1 000 and the penalty for withdrawals within the first 12 months are characteristic features of RSA Retail Savings Bonds.

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the advantages of the form of investment identified in QUESTION 2.3.1 (Government/RSA Retail Savings Bonds).
subQuestions.memoText:
Advantages of Government/RSA Retail Savings Bonds (1 mark per √, max 4; accept relevant facts even if 2.3.1 was incorrectly identified):
- Guaranteed returns √ as the interest rate is fixed for the whole investment period √.
- Interest rates are market related √ and attract more investors √.
- Interest can be received twice a year √ making it a viable investment option √.
- Easily accessible √ as cash may be withdrawn after the first twelve months √.
- Low-risk/safe investment √ as it is invested with the SA Government which cannot be liquidated √.
- Affordable type of investment √ for all levels of income earners including pensioners √.
- Easily/conveniently obtained electronically √ from any Post Office/National Treasury √.
- No charges/costs/commissions payable √ on this investment √.
- Interest is usually higher √ than on fixed deposits √.
- Retail bonds are listed √ on the capital bond markets/JSE √.
- Minors may invest with help of a legal guardian √ encouraging saving from a young age √.
[Max 4 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the difference between limited liability and unlimited liability.
subQuestions.memoText:
Difference between limited and unlimited liability (1 mark per √, submax 2 each side, max 4; table not required; max 2 if difference is unclear):

Limited liability:
- Losses are limited √ to the amount that the owner invested in the business √.
- Owner's personal assets are protected √ against the debts of the business √.
- Applicable to forms of ownership/companies √ that have a separate legal entity/personality √.

Unlimited liability:
- The liability of the owner to pay debts/claims √ is not limited to the business only √.
- Owner's personal assets may be seized √ to pay for the debts of the business √.
- Applicable to sole trader/proprietorship and partnership √ that do not have a separate legal entity/personality √.
[Max 4 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss the impact of the laissez-faire/free-reign leadership style.
subQuestions.memoText:
Impact of laissez-faire/free-reign leadership style (1 mark per √, max 4):

Positives/Advantages
- Employees are allowed to make decisions √ in their own areas of expertise/work/methods √.
- Subordinates have maximum freedom √ and can work independently/without consulting the leader √.
- Subordinates are motivated √ when leaders trust their abilities/skills √.
- Authority is delegated √ which can be motivating/empowering and increase productivity √.
- Subordinates are experts √ and know what they want/can take responsibility √.
- Suitable for coaching/mentoring √ to motivate employees to achieve more √.
- Competent employees experience personal growth √ and become self-reliant/confident √.
- Individual team members √ may improve/develop leadership skills √.

AND/OR Negatives/Disadvantages
- Lack of clear direction/leadership √ may demotivate employees √.
- Employees held responsible for their own work √ which may lead to underperformance √.
- Could lead to conflict √ when some team members act as leaders/dictate to others √.
- Workers must solve their own conflicts/disagreements √ without involving leaders √.
- Productivity may be compromised √ with lack of tight control over deadlines √.
- Productivity might be low √ if employees lack knowledge/skills √.
[Max 4 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Read the scenario: 'Qushu Limited (QL) requested Sam, the financial manager, to present audited financial statements to various stakeholders. Sam used a special pen to make notes while images were being displayed. The audience were given hard copies of his presentation for future reference.' Identify TWO visual aids used by Sam. subQuestions.memoText:

Motivation: Sam used a special pen to make notes while images were being displayed. √

2. Hand-outs/Flyers/Brochures √√
Motivation: The audience were given hard copies of his presentation for future reference. √

[Submax: visual aids 4; motivations 2; Max 6 marks]
subQuestions.topic: Presentation of Business Information / Visual Aids

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss any TWO principles of insurance.
subQuestions.memoText:
Principles of insurance (mark first TWO only; each principle = 2 marks for naming + 1 mark per discussion point; submax 3 per principle; max 6):

Indemnification/Indemnity √√
- Usually applies to short-term insurance — insured is compensated for specified/proven harm/loss √.
- Insurer agrees to compensate the insured for damages/losses specified in the contract, in return for premiums √.
- Protects the insured against the specified event √.
- Pay-outs are made only if there is proof the specified event took place/proof of loss amount √.
- The amount is limited to the provable loss/damage, even if the policy amount is higher √.
- The insured must be placed in the same position as before the loss / may not profit from insurance √.

Security/Certainty √√
- Applies to long-term insurance where the insurer pays an agreed-upon amount in the event of loss of life √.
- A predetermined amount is paid when the insured reaches a predetermined age/is injured by a predetermined event √.
- Aims to provide financial security at retirement/to dependents of the deceased √.

Utmost good faith √√
- Insured must be honest in supplying details when entering the contract √.
- Both parties must disclose all relevant facts √.
- Insured must disclose everything that may affect the extent of risk √.
- Information supplied when claiming must be accurate/true √.

Insurable interest √√
- Insured must prove they will suffer financial loss if the insured object is damaged/lost √.
- An insurable interest must be expressed in financial terms √.
- Insured must have a legal relationship with the insured object √.
[Max 6 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Advise presenters on the aspects that should be considered when designing a multimedia presentation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Aspects to consider when designing a multimedia presentation (2 marks each, max 6):
- Start with the text/heading which forms the basis of the presentation.
- Select the background to complement/enhance the text.
- Choose images that may help to communicate the message.
- Include/create graphics to assist the information conveyed.
- Add special effects/sound/pictures/animation to make it interesting.
- Create hyperlinks to allow quick access to other files/documents/video clips.
- Use legible font and font size so that it is easy to see/read.
- Keep slides/images/graphs/font simple by not mixing different styles/colours.
- Make sure there are no language and spelling errors.
- Use bright colours to increase visibility.
- Structure information in a logical sequence so audience can easily follow.
- Limit information on each slide by using key words and not full sentences.
[Max 6 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Name any TWO social rights of employees in the workplace.
subQuestions.memoText:
Social rights of employees (mark first TWO only, 1 mark each):
- Clean water
- Education
- Protection
- Health care
[Max 2 marks]
subQuestions.topic: Human Rights / Social Rights in the Workplace

subQuestions.questionText: Outline the correct procedures to deal with grievances in the workplace.
subQuestions.memoText:
Procedures to deal with grievances (2 marks each, max 6; procedures may be in any order):
- Aggrieved employee verbally reports the incident/grievance to his/her supervisor/manager.
- Supervisor/manager must resolve the issue within 3 to 5 working days.
- If unresolved, the employee may take it to the next level of management.
- The employee may move to a more formal process by lodging the grievance in writing/completing a grievance form.
- The employee must receive a written reply to the written grievance.
- A grievance hearing/meeting must be held with all relevant parties.
- Minutes must be recorded and any resolution recorded on the formal grievance form.
- If still unsatisfied, the employee may refer the matter to the highest level of management.
- Top management arranges a meeting with all relevant parties.
- Minutes of the meeting must be filed and the outcome recorded on the form.
- If still unsatisfied, the employee may refer the matter to the CCMA for a final decision.
- The matter may be referred to the Labour Court/Labour Appeal Court/Constitutional Court if needed.
[Max 6 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the human right promoted by Meadridge Landscaping in the following statement: 'Employees' personal information is kept confidential.'
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Privacy (2 marks)
Keeping employees' personal information confidential is a direct application of the right to privacy in the workplace.

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the human right promoted by Meadridge Landscaping in the following statement: 'Meadridge Landscaping ensures that the workplace environment is free from hazardous products.'
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Safety, security and protection of life (2 marks)
Ensuring a workplace environment free from hazardous products promotes the right to safety, security and protection of life.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain ways in which businesses can deal with taxation/tax evasion as a type of unethical business practice.
subQuestions.memoText:
Dealing with taxation/tax evasion (1 mark per √, max 4):
- VAT needs to be charged √ on VAT-able items √.
- Submit the correct tax returns √ to SARS on time √.
- All products correctly invoiced √ and recorded √.
- Disclose all sources of income √ for tax payment purposes √.
- Keep abreast with the latest SARS regulations √ and tax laws √.
- Businesses that have evaded tax √ should apply for amnesty and declare income √.
- Effective systems √ to determine the appropriate amount of tax to be paid √.
- Keep accurate records √ of income statements/financial transactions √.
- Payroll must reflect accurate deductions √ according to the progressive tax system √.
- All financial records √ must be checked and audited √.
[Max 4 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss any TWO problem-solving steps.
subQuestions.memoText:
Problem-solving steps (mark first TWO only; each step = 2 marks for naming + 1 mark per discussion point; submax 3 per step; max 6; steps may be in any order):

Identify the problem √√
- Acknowledge that there is a problem √.
- Identify the exact problem √.
- Break down the problem into smaller/separate parts √.

Define the problem √√
- Name the problem by stating exactly what it is √.
- Find different ways of defining the problem √.
- Define the possible causes of the problem √.
- The nature of the problem must be precise √.
- Gather as much information as possible to establish the cause √.

Identify possible solutions √√
- Identify all different possible solutions √.
- Use creative thinking strategies to generate solutions √.
- Focus on generating as many ways as possible √.
- Collect ideas and find the best one/decide on a strategy √.

Evaluate alternative solutions √√
- Use critical evaluation and analytical skills to evaluate each solution √.
- Consider the advantages and disadvantages of each alternative √.

Select the most appropriate solution √√
- Set criteria for the best solution (time/cost/risk) √.
- Identify the most relevant solution √.
- The solution should match the size and resources of the business √.
- If not appropriate, go back to defining the problem √.

Develop an action plan √√
- Arrange resources and delegate tasks √.
- Establish a time line and set deadlines √.

Implement the action plan √√
- Carry out the planned actions √.
- Communicate delegated tasks/deadlines to employees √.

Monitor implementation √√
- Test the action plan continuously to improve effectiveness √.
- Check progress against the objectives of the plan √.

Evaluate the implemented action plan √√
- Assess whether the problem has been solved partially or entirely √.
- Unresolved problems should be re-formulated/reviewed for an improved plan √.
[Max 6 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Read the scenario: 'African Designers (AD) apply the King Code principles for good corporate governance. AD developed remedial programmes to reduce air and water pollution which will protect the environment.' Identify the King Code principle applied by AD. Motivate your answer by quoting from the scenario above.

King Code principle: Responsibility √√ (2 marks)
Motivation: AD developed remedial programmes to reduce air and water pollution which will protect the environment. √ (1 mark)
NOTE: Do not award marks for the motivation if the King Code principle was incorrectly identified.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain any ONE other King Code principle for good corporate governance that AD could apply.
subQuestions.memoText:
Application of one other King Code principle (mark FIRST ONE only; principle 2 + explanation 1; submax 3; do not award marks for 'responsibility'; max 3):

Transparency √√
- Decisions/actions must be clear to all stakeholders √.
- Staffing and processes should be open and transparent √.
- Employees/shareholders/directors should be aware of employment policies √.
- Auditing and other reports must be accurate/available to stakeholders √.
- Regular audits should be done to determine effectiveness √.
- Business deals should be conducted openly with no hint of dishonesty √.
- Shareholders should be given details of voting rights before/at AGM √.
- The board must report on negative and positive impacts on community/environment √.
- The board should ensure ethics are effectively implemented √.

OR

Accountability √√
- Regular communication between management and stakeholders √.
- Appoint internal and external auditors to audit financial statements √.
- Board should ensure ethics are effectively implemented √.
- Businesses should be accountable/responsible for decisions/actions √.
- Present accurate annual reports to shareholders at the AGM √.
- Top management should ensure other levels are clear about roles and responsibilities √.
[Max 3 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss storming as a stage of team development.
subQuestions.memoText:
Storming as a stage of team development (1 mark per √, max 6):
- Teams go through a period of unease/conflict √ after formation √.
- Different ideas from team members √ will compete for consideration √.
- Team members open up to each other √ and confront each other's ideas √.
- Tension/struggle/arguments occur √ and upset team members √ / There may be power struggles √ for the position of team leader √.
- In some instances storming can be resolved quickly √, in others the team never leaves this stage √.
- Many teams fail at this stage √ as they are not focused on their task √.
- This phase can become destructive/lower motivation √ if allowed to get out of control √.
- This stage is necessary/important √ for the growth of the team √.
- Some team members tolerate each other √ to survive this stage √.
[Max 6 marks]
subQuestions.topic: Team Performance / Stages of Team Development

subQuestions.questionText: Recommend ways in which businesses could deal with language as a diversity issue in the workplace.
subQuestions.memoText:
Dealing with language as a diversity issue (2 marks each, max 6):
- Provide training in the official language of the business.
- No worker should feel excluded in meetings conducted in one language only.
- Employ an interpreter so everyone can fully understand what is being said.
- All business contracts should be in easy-to-understand language and available in the language of choice for relevant parties signing.
- Business may specify that all communications be in one specific language only and expect employees to have a certain level of fluency in that language.
[Max 6 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: State any FOUR factors that should be considered when making investment decisions.
subQuestions.memoText:
Factors to consider when making investment decisions (mark first FOUR only, 1 mark each):

subQuestions.questionText: Outline the functions of the Johannesburg Securities Exchange (JSE).
subQuestions.memoText:
Functions of the JSE (2 marks each, max 4):
- Gives opportunities to financial institutions (e.g. insurers) to invest surplus funds in shares.
- Serves as a barometer/indicator of economic conditions in SA.
- Keeps investors informed by publishing share prices daily.
- Acts as a link between investors and public companies.
- Shares are valued and assessed by experts.
- Small investors are invited to take part in the economy via buying/selling shares.
- Venture capital market is made possible on the open market.
- Strict investment rules ensure a disciplined/orderly market.
- Raises primary capital by encouraging new investments in listed companies.
- Mobilises funds of insurance companies and other institutions.
- Regulates the market for trading shares.
- Plans, researches and advises on investment possibilities.
- Ensures the market operates transparently.
- Provides protection for investors via rules/legislation.
- Encourages short-term investment as shares can be sold any time.
- Facilitates electronic trading via STRATE / channels resources into productive activities.
- Enhances job creation and increases economic growth/development.
[Max 4 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Read the scenario: 'Sandy, the owner of Sandy Bakery, wants to use her additional income to expand her business. She decided to buy shares in Bio Ltd.' subQuestions.memoText:

Motivation: Sandy, the owner of Sandy Bakery, wants to use her additional income to expand her business. √

Motivation: She decided to buy shares in Bio Ltd. √

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the factors that must be considered when preparing for a presentation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Factors to consider when preparing for a presentation (1 mark per √, max 6):
- Clear purpose/intentions/objectives √ and main points of the presentation √.
- The main aims should be captured √ in the introduction/opening statement √.
- Information presented should be relevant √ and accurate √.
- Be fully conversant with the content/objectives √ of the presentation √.
- Background/diversity/size/pre-knowledge of the audience √ to determine appropriate visual aids √.
- Prepare a rough draft √ with a logical structure (introduction, body, conclusion) √.
- The conclusion must summarise key facts √ and how it relates to objectives √.
- Create visual aids/graphics that consolidate information/facts √ to be conveyed √.
- Find out about the venue √ such as equipment available/generators as backup √.
- The time frame should be considered √ such as 15 minutes allowed √.
- Rehearse the presentation √ to gain confidence and ensure effective time management √.
- Prepare for the feedback session √ by anticipating possible questions/comments √.
[Max 6 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Elaborate on the meaning of professional behaviour.
subQuestions.memoText:
Meaning of professional behaviour (1 mark per √, max 4):
- Professional behaviour is a certain standard of behaviour/specific level of competence √ that adheres to an ethical code of conduct √.
- Provides guidelines √ on employee's appearance/communication/responsibility √.
- Ability/skills expected of a person √ employed for the job √ / Applicable for a job/profession √ done for payment √.
- Focuses on upholding the reputation √ of a business/profession √.
- Refers/clarifies what is right/wrong √ and acceptable behaviour in the business √.
- Applying the code of conduct √ of that profession/business √.
[Max 4 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how businesses should handle conflict in the workplace.
subQuestions.memoText:
Handling conflict in the workplace (1 mark per √, max 4):
- Acknowledge that there is conflict √ between employers/employees/parties √.
- Identify the cause √ of the conflict √.
- Arrange pre-negotiations where workers/complainants are allowed √ to state their case/views separately √.
- Arrange time and place for negotiations √ where all employees involved are present √.
- Arrange a meeting √ between conflicting employers/employees √.
- Make intentions for the intervention clear √ so parties feel at ease √.
- Each party has the opportunity to express √ his/her opinions/feelings √.
- Conflicting parties may recognise that views differ √ during the meeting √.
- Analyse/evaluate the cause(s) √ by breaking it down into parts √.
- Blame shifting should be avoided √ — joint effort should be made √.
- Direct conflicting parties √ towards finding solutions √.
- Devise/brainstorm possible ways √ of resolving the conflict √.
- Conflicting parties agree on criteria √ to evaluate alternatives √.
- Select/implement √ the best solution √.
- Provide opportunities for parties √ to agree on the best solution √.
- Evaluate/follow up √ on the implementation of solutions √.
- Monitor progress √ to ensure conflict has been resolved √.
- Source experts on conflict handling √ from outside the business √.
[Max 4 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Explain other ways in which KE can deal with unemployment as a socio-economic issue.

subQuestions.questionText: Evaluate the impact of corporate social responsibility (CSR) on businesses.
subQuestions.memoText:
Impact of CSR on businesses (1 mark per √, max 6):

Positives/Advantages
- May attract experienced employees/increase pool of skilled labour √ which could increase productivity √.
- Positive/improved image √ as the business looks after employees and acts responsibly √.
- Competitive advantage √ resulting in good publicity/improved reputation √.
- Promotes customer loyalty √ resulting in more sales √.
- CSR projects may be used as a marketing strategy √ to promote products √.
- Businesses enjoy goodwill/support √ of communities √.
- Promotes teamwork √ within businesses √.
- Helps attract investors √ due to increased profits/income/growth √.
- Tax advantages √ such as tax reduction/rebates √.
- Government less likely to enforce legislation √ on businesses voluntarily participating √.
- Employees feel they are making a difference √ working for the business √.
- Helps retain staff/lower turnover √ as health and safety are considered √.
- Improves health of employees √ through focused projects √.

AND/OR Negatives/Disadvantages
- Customers may not buy products/services √ resulting in decreased sales √.
- Small/medium enterprises find it difficult √ to implement CSR programmes √.
- Detailed reports must be drawn up √ which can be time-consuming √.
- Social spending reduces business/economic efficiency √ making it less competitive √.
- Social involvement is funded from profits √ which could have benefited customers/reduced prices √.
- CSR distracts focus √ from core business functions √.
- Difficult √ to adhere to legislation governing CSR √.
- Increases financial risk √ as programmes cost money and may impact profits √.
- Difficult to accurately measure √ effectiveness of social investment √.
- Hard to determine exact community needs √ — may result in fruitless expenditure √.
- Most managers are not trained √ to handle social programmes √.
- Employees may spend more time on CSR projects √ instead of core duties √.
- Providing goods/services that meet needs √ is, to some, already socially responsible √.
- Shareholders may receive less dividends √ as profits are spent on CSR √.
- Some shareholders may withdraw support √ feeling social issues are government's responsibility √.
[Max 6 marks]

questions.title: SECTION C – QUESTION 5: BUSINESS VENTURES (Management and Leadership) – Essay

subQuestions.questionText:
Businesses agree that leaders' personal attitude play an important role in successful leadership. Some businesses apply the democratic leadership style whereas others apply the autocratic leadership style. The situational and transformational leadership theories provide guidelines on the application of leadership styles. Certain situations require businesses to apply the transactional leadership style.

Write an essay on management and leadership in which you include the following aspects:
• Outline the role of personal attitude in successful leadership.
• Explain the differences between democratic and autocratic leadership styles.
• Discuss the following leadership theories:
  o Situational
  o Transformational
• Recommend situations in which the transactional leadership style could be applied in the workplace.
subQuestions.memoText:
ESSAY MARK BREAKDOWN: Content 32 + Insight 8 = 40

INTRODUCTION (max 2; any 2 x 1):
- Personal attitude of managers/leaders plays an important role in encouraging harmonious work.
- Democratic and autocratic leadership styles require sound knowledge of employees' skills and abilities.
- Situational leadership theory helps leaders adjust strategies to employee needs.
- Transformational leadership theory encourages employees to develop themselves.
- Transactional leadership style focuses on supervision/organisation/performance via clear guidelines.

ROLE OF PERSONAL ATTITUDE IN SUCCESSFUL LEADERSHIP (max 10; 2 marks each):
- Positive attitude releases leadership potential for personal growth.
- A leader's good attitude can influence the success of the business.
- Leaders must know their strengths and weaknesses to apply leadership styles effectively.
- A great leader understands that the right attitude sets the right atmosphere.
- Leaders' attitude may influence employees'/teams' thoughts/behaviour.
- Leaders should model the behaviour they want to see in team members.
- Successful leaders consider abilities/skills to allocate tasks/roles effectively.
- Enthusiasm produces confidence and inspires harder work.
- Positive attitude is critical — good leaders persist despite difficulties.
- Successful employees and leaders have a constant desire to achieve personal/professional success.
- Leaders with a positive attitude know there is always more to learn/grow.

DIFFERENCES BETWEEN DEMOCRATIC AND AUTOCRATIC LEADERSHIP STYLES (max 12; 2 marks per side, submax 6 each; table not required; max 6 if differences unclear):

Democratic:
- Leader involves employees in decision making.
- Clear/two-way communication ensures group commitment to decisions.
- People-oriented — employees' feelings and opinions are considered.
- Workers feel empowered as they are involved in decision making.
- Useful when leader depends on inputs of experienced followers.
- Handles conflict by involving followers in finding the best solution.

Autocratic:
- Leader takes all decisions alone without involving employees.
- Line of command/communication is clear/top-down — followers know exactly what to do.
- Task-oriented — opinions of employees are not considered.
- New employees feel confident/safe as strong leadership is provided.
- Useful in a crisis/urgent situation (e.g. after an accident/tight deadline).
- Handles conflict by telling followers what they should do.

LEADERSHIP THEORIES (max 16):

5.4.1 Situational leadership theory (submax 8; 1 mark per √)
- Different leadership characteristics √ are needed for different situations √.
- The task/situation dictates the leadership style √, so leaders are adaptable/flexible/self-assured √.
- Effective application enables leaders √ to accomplish goals √.
- Relationships with employees √ based on mutual trust/respect/loyalty/integrity/honesty √.
- Leaders can analyse the situation/get most suitable people in the right positions √ to complete tasks √.
- Leaders analyse group members/objectives/time constraints √ to adopt a relevant style √.
- May lead to conflict when leaders use different styles √ in different situations √.
- Success depends on the relationship √ between leader and followers √.

5.4.2 Transformational leadership theory (submax 8; 1 mark per √)
- Suitable for a dynamic environment √ where change could be drastic √.
- The passion/vision/personality of leaders inspires followers √ to change expectations/perceptions/motivation √.
- Strategic-thinking leaders develop a long-term vision √ and sell it to subordinates √.
- Leaders have the trust/respect/admiration √ of followers √.
- Promotes intellectual stimulation/creative thinking/problem solving √ leading to growth/development/success √.
- Followers are coached/mentored/emotionally supported √ through change so they can share ideas freely √.
- Encourages followers √ to explore/try new opportunities √.
- Leaders lead by example √ and make workers interested in their work √.
- Leaders have strong/charismatic personalities √ and motivate staff to achieve results √.
- Enables employees to take greater ownership √ and recognise strengths/weaknesses √.

SITUATIONS WHERE TRANSACTIONAL LEADERSHIP STYLE COULD BE APPLIED (max 8; 2 marks each):
- The business wants to maximise employee performance.
- Deadlines have to be met on short notice/under pressure.
- Workers have low morale.
- The strategies/business structures are clear and do not have to change.
- Productivity levels are very low/not according to targets.

CONCLUSION (max 2; any 1 x 2):
- Leaders with a positive attitude may experience increased productivity as employees may be happy in the workplace.
- Leaders can apply democratic and autocratic styles interchangeably depending on employees' attitudes.
- Situational leadership theory requires leaders to be experts in diagnosing employees' strengths and weaknesses.
- Transformational leadership gives employees independence to make decisions and support new approaches.
- Effective transactional leadership maximises knowledge and support of employees to benefit the business.

INSIGHT (8 marks): Layout (2), Analysis/Interpretation (2), Synthesis (2), Originality/Examples (2). LASO – allocate 2 if all met, 1 if some met, 0 if none met.

TOTAL: 32 (content) + 8 (insight) = 40

questions.title: SECTION C – QUESTION 6: BUSINESS ROLES (Creative Thinking and Problem-solving) – Essay

subQuestions.questionText:
Creative thinking allows businesses to be innovative in their approach and take advantage of viable business opportunities. This requires them to create an environment that promotes creative thinking in the workplace. Successful businesses know the impact of the Delphi technique and the nominal group technique in solving business problems. Many businesses apply brainstorming when faced with challenging tasks.

Write an essay on creative thinking and problem-solving in which you include the following aspects:
• Outline the advantages of creative thinking in the workplace.
• Explain ways in which businesses can create an environment that promotes creative thinking in the workplace.
• Discuss the impact of the following problem-solving techniques:
  o Delphi technique
  o Nominal group technique
• Advise businesses on how they can apply brainstorming to solve complex business problems.
subQuestions.memoText:
ESSAY MARK BREAKDOWN: Content 32 + Insight 8 = 40

INTRODUCTION (max 2; any 2 x 1):
- Creative thinking enables businesses to improve products and develop new ways of doing things.
- An environment that promotes creative thinking enables employees to unleash their potential.
- Businesses apply the Delphi technique to eliminate conflicting ideas which may delay problem solving.
- Businesses use the nominal group technique to obtain different ideas/viewpoints.
- Brainstorming allows businesses to develop and record ideas for future challenges.

ADVANTAGES OF CREATIVE THINKING IN THE WORKPLACE (max 12; 2 marks each):
- Better/unique/unconventional ideas/solutions are generated.
- Competitive advantage if unusual/unique solutions are implemented.
- Broadens range of solutions when solving complex problems.
- Productivity increases — multiple ideas use time/money effectively.
- Managers/employees gain confidence and live up to full potential.
- Managers become better leaders, handling change creatively.
- Develops a new outlook applicable to any task.
- More positive attitudes — feeling of contribution to problem solving.
- Improves motivation, leading to higher job satisfaction.
- Sense of accomplishment — employees don't resist the process.
- Helps keep up with fast-changing technology, increasing market share.
- Stimulates initiative — employees pushed out of their comfort zone.
- Creativity may lead to new inventions, improving standard of living/attracting investors.
- Continuous improvement of product development for growth.

WAYS TO CREATE AN ENVIRONMENT THAT PROMOTES CREATIVE THINKING (max 12; 1 mark per √):
- Encourage alternative ways √ of working/doing things √.
- Emphasise importance of creative thinking √ — staff know management wants to hear ideas √.
- Make time for brainstorming sessions √ to generate new ideas / regular workshops √.
- Place suggestion boxes √ and keep communication channels open √.
- Train staff in innovative techniques √ such as creative problem solving/mind-mapping/lateral thinking √.
- Encourage job swops √ within the organisation √ / Study how other businesses √ are doing things √.
- Respond enthusiastically to all ideas √ and never let anyone feel less important √.
- Reward creativity √ with reward schemes √ / Introduce incentives √ for creative ideas √.
- Provide a working environment conducive to creativity √ free from distractions/high noise √.

IMPACT OF PROBLEM-SOLVING TECHNIQUES (max 12):

6.4.1 Delphi technique (submax 6; 1 mark per √)
Positives/Advantages
- Use a group of experts √ without bringing them together √.
- Experts give clear ideas/solutions √ to improve productivity/profitability √.
- Information from experts √ used to solve complex problems √.
- Honest/credible opinions √ as experts have no direct/personal interest √.
- Conflict avoided √ if all employees are knowledgeable/qualified √.
- Dominating employees can't take over the process √ since they don't form part of it √.
- Reduces noise levels √ since there are no group discussions √.

AND/OR Negatives/Disadvantages
- Expensive technique √ due to high admin costs √.
- Time consuming/complicated √ to analyse data from experts √.
- Not all experts are willing/interested √ to give feedback √.
- Some experts may not have in-depth knowledge √ of certain topics √.
- Experts' suggestions may not be considered √ — consensus may not be reached √.

6.4.2 Nominal group technique (submax 6; 1 mark per √)
Positives/Advantages
- Time to think about the question in silence √ before responding √.
- Each member has a chance to participate √ without interference √.
- Voting is anonymous √ and may be more reliable/honest √.
- Everyone given opportunity to contribute √, avoiding domination √.
- Generates and clarifies many ideas quickly √ and prioritises them democratically √.
- Encourages confronting issues √ via constructive problem solving √.
- Strong technique for preventing conformity √ to group pressure √.

AND/OR Negatives/Disadvantages
- Minimises discussion √ — does not allow full development of ideas √.
- Ideas may not converge √ and cannot lead to the same solution √.
- Suggestions may not be as creative √ as group brainstorming √.
- Time consuming √ as each member must present √.
- Hard to implement effectively in large groups √ unless carefully planned √.
- Requires extended advance preparation √ — cannot be spontaneous √.
- Good ideas can be voted out √ — potential not developed further √.
- Small groups limit participation √ and are pre-selected √.

APPLICATION OF BRAINSTORMING (max 10; 2 marks each):
- State/define the business problem clearly so all participants understand it.
- Members state possible causes of the problems.
- Set a time limit for each session.
- Record/write ideas where all participants can see them / share online (E-brainstorming).
- Use each suggestion to inspire new thoughts/ideas.
- Do not judge/criticise/discuss ideas — generate as many as possible quickly.
- All members of the group randomly make suggestions.
- The group rates ideas according to usefulness/success/difficulty/cost.
- The group evaluates all ideas, combining similar ones / draws up a refined list.
- Discuss a plan of action for implementing the best ideas.

CONCLUSION (max 2; any 1 x 2):
- Creative thinking enables continuous research on latest market trends.
- Employees in a creative environment are more committed, lowering voluntary turnover.
- Delphi technique allows informed decisions through expert input.
- Businesses should invest time in nominal group technique — all employees give input.
- Brainstorming allows extreme responses to assist the thought process of other team members.

INSIGHT (8 marks): Layout (2), Analysis/Interpretation (2), Synthesis (2), Originality/Examples (2). LASO – allocate 2 if all met, 1 if some met, 0 if none met.

TOTAL: 32 (content) + 8 (insight) = 40
